title: Shalmaneser III invades Syria
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). Dated only by the Generations books cited below; no tier 1–4 chronology covers this event.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 2: CFAH Reply to Beckman (Griffith & White, Part 2): 853 BC (Battle of Qarqar, Shalmaneser III year 6). Sort changed by the Reply to Beckman pass (2026-11-13): was provisional 853 BC.

chronologies.date: 853 BC (Battle of Qarqar, Shalmaneser III year 6)
chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "A Reply to Beckman’s Defense of Thiele’s Chronology, Part 2: An Objectivist Answer to the Assyrian Synchronisms," OSF preprint v2.10 (2025), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/DT6GX, section “Hazael”, p. 13; Table 1, p. 36
chronologies.note: Shalmaneser III invades Syria and fights the Battle of Qarqar. Griffith & White read the “Acha-abbu Sirila-a-a” of the Kurkh Monolith as an Israelite general under Jehoahaz, not King Ahab, and Hadad-ezer as Ben-Hadad, son of Hazael.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 10 "The Assyrian Empire: Power by Cruelty (1200–612 BC)", PDF p. 324 (printed p. 323)
chronologies.note: Timeline Review. The text (p. 305) speaks of invasions from 898 BC and a siege of Damascus in 886 BC.
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "853 BC" (PDF p. 358): the same date.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 14 "Old Babylon–The Rising Threats to Israel", PDF p. 358 (printed p. 344)
chronologies.note: Battle of Qarqar; also p. 346 and the table on p. 380.

chronologies.citation: Morecraft, A Christian Survey of World History, p. 42 (PDF p. 50)
chronologies.note: From the book's "Ancient Empires" pages (credited in an image to Daily Bible Study, keyway.ca). Reign of Shalmaneser III.
